The 30-share BSE benchmark Sensex jumped 7,976.46 points, or 10.71 per cent till November 23.

Following the bullish trend in equities, the market capitalisation of BSE-listed companies has surged by Rs 34.61 lakh crore to Rs 5,08,98,444.87 crore (USD 5.48 trillion) this month.

Foreign investors have emerged as a major driver behind markets rally, with net investments crossing the Rs 1 lakh crore mark to reach Rs 1.27 lakh crore in November so far, marking the highest-ever monthly inflow.

The strong inflows come after Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) withdrew Rs 34,843 crore in October and Rs 35,861 crore in September, according to data available with the NSDL.

The sharp rally in the market is remarkable after the Sensex hit its one-year low of 71,292.88 on October 1 this year. The BSE Sensex is 3,723 points away from its all-time high of 86,159.02 hit on December 1 last year.

Last week, the BSE benchmark jumped 2,327.26 points, or 2.85 per cent, and the Nifty climbed 656.3 points, or 2.61 per cent.

Markets faced sharp profit-booking on Monday, declining nearly 2 per cent, following a four-week rally.

The Indian stock market will remain closed on Tuesday, 24 November, on account of Prakash Gurpurb Sri Guru Nanak Dev, also known as Guru Nanak Jayanti. While equity markets will remain shut, trading arrangements across commodity exchanges will differ. The Multi-Commodity Exchange of India (MCX MCX will suspend trading during its morning session, from 9 am to 5 pm, on Tuesday, 24 November. However, the exchange will reopen for the evening session, with trading scheduled from 5 pm to 11:30 pm, according to its website. NCDEX, on the other hand, will remain closed throughout the day. This means traders in commodity markets should check the exchange-wise schedule before placing orders, as the holiday will not affect all segments in the same way. Following the 24 November closure for Guru Nanak Jayanti, the next scheduled trading holiday for the BSE and NSE will be on 25 December, on account of Christmas. Of the 16 stock market holidays scheduled for 2026, 14 have already been observed. The exchanges were closed twice in April — on 3 April for Good Friday and 14 April for Dr B.R. Ambedkar Jayanti. Other holidays during the year included Maharashtra Day on 1 May, Bakri Id on 28 May, Muharram on 26 June and Ganesh Chaturthi on 14 September. Markets also remained shut on 2 October for Mahatma Gandhi Jayanti and 20 October for Dussehra. The most recent holiday before Tuesday was 10 November, for Diwali. With the 24 November holiday, only the Christmas closure remains on the 2026 trading calendar. The market holiday comes at a time when Indian equities are drawing renewed interest from foreign investors and moving closer to their previous record highs. The Nifty 50 is now around 2% below its all-time high of 26,373.20, while the Sensex is less than 3% away from its record peak of 86,159. A sharp turnaround in foreign institutional investor (FII) flows has been a major driver of the recent rally. Foreign investors, who had been among the biggest sellers in Indian equities, have extended their buying streak to 15 consecutive sessions. Their net purchases in domestic equities have crossed ₹1.3 lakh crore so far in November. Foreign investors have been reallocating funds away from global artificial intelligence-linked trades towards India's liquid and relatively reasonably valued large-cap stocks, particularly banking shares. Private lenders have helped push the banking index to successive record highs. A stronger rupee, softer crude oil prices and resilient second-quarter earnings have further supported the positive sentiment towards Indian equities. With the benchmark indices nearing record levels and foreign inflows gathering pace, investors will be watching whether the rally can regain momentum when trading resumes after the Guru Nanak Jayanti holiday. Nagaraj Shetti, Senior Technical Research Analyst at HDFC Securities, said the market witnessed sharp profit-booking on Monday after a strong rally over the past few weeks. The Nifty 50 slipped from highs near the 26,000 mark and ended the session nearly 450 points lower. He noted that the daily chart formed a long bearish candle after the index opened higher. The candle engulfed the previous session's long bullish candle, indicating a potential shift in market sentiment. According to Shetti, the pattern resembles a Bearish Dark Cloud Cover, which signals a possible short-term downside reversal. However, the pattern will be confirmed only if the market sees further weakness in the subsequent session. Monday's trading range stood at around 648 points. Shetti said the Nifty 50's short-term trend has turned bearish following its sharp upward move. However, he believes the ongoing correction could be short-lived, with the market likely to attempt a recovery from lower levels. He identified 25,000 as an immediate support level, while a decisive rebound could face strong resistance around 26,000. *Disclaimer: This story is for educational purposes only. **Silver Price Today: **Silver rate today in India is around ₹1,54,000 per kg after a strong rebound of over ₹6,000 on Monday. Barring this rebound, the precious white metal price in India was around ₹1 lakh below the August 2026 high of around ₹2.50 lakh per kg, which means the silver rate today in India is down by around ₹1 lakh in three months. US bond yields sustaining at higher levels, a strong US Dollar (USD) against the major six global currencies, buzz for a US Fed rate hike, and appreciation in the Indian Rupee are some of the major reasons for the silver price crash in India. According to market experts, the silver rate today in India has crucial support at ₹1,40,000. Breaking below this support on a closing basis would mean further downside towards ₹1,20,000 and ₹1,00,000 per kg. In the international market, silver price today has crucial support placed at $38/oz. Breaking below this support would open the downside probability of $34/oz and $30/oz. They said that silver prices would be considered bottomed out if they break above ₹1,90,000 per kg in the Indian market and above $52/oz in the international market. Highlighting the reasons for the silver price crash, Anuj Gupta, a SEBI-registered market expert, said, “The downside trend in the MCX silver rates and the COMEX silver price today can be attributed to these three reasons: US bond yields sustaining at elevated levels; Indian Rupee appreciating against the US Dollar (USD) from around 98 to 92.50 levels, and buzz for the US Fed rate hike.” Pointing towards the Indian Rupee's appreciation, Anuj Gupta said, “The Indian Rupee has ascended from around 98 per USD levels to around 92.50 per USD levels in the last three months. This worked as a taper for the domestic upside trigger for the precious white metal even when the global triggers were supportive for an upside move in silver prices.” Pointing towards the buzz for the US Fed rate hike in upcoming US Fed meeting, the SEBI-registered market expert said, “Due to the renewed fear of US inflation, speculations are high about the US Fed rate hike in the December 2026 US Fed meeting. The market is estimating the US CPI inflation print for October 2026 to edge higher from 3.10% to 3.20%. If the expectations turn reality on Wednesday, it will fuel the fear of inflation more, putting pressure on the US Fed to go for a rate hike in upcoming FOMC meeting.” Anuj Gupta said that US 10-year bond yield came blow 5% to 4.923%, but it much above the alarming 4.50% levels. A disappointing US inflation data would mean US Fed rate hike, which will strengthen US Dollar, which is already at the 19-month high. So, the US CPI data would be important, but as per the market expectations, a disappointing data would trigger buying in the US dollar and US bonds, which will be highly detrimental for the silver price recovery. Advising investors to remain vigilant about the key support for silver prices in India and in the international market, Anuj Gupta said, “Silver rates today in India has crucial support at ₹1,40,000. Breaking below this support would open the downside targets of ₹1,20,000 and ₹1,00,000 per kg. Similarly, in the international market, silver price today has crucial support at $38 per ounce. Breaking below this support may open the window of opportunity for the downside targets of $34 per ounce and $30 per ounce.” “If the COMEX silver price sustains above $38/oz and breaks above $52/oxz, then we can assume that the precious white metal has bottomed out. In the Indian markets, if the silver price breaks above ₹1,90,000 per kg, then we can assume that the precious white metal has bottomed out in the domestic market,” Anuj Gupta said. Speaking on the outlook for the silver prices in the international market, Ponmudi R, CEO at Enrich Money, said, “The near-term bias remains cautious, with a sustained move above $43.50 needed to strengthen the recovery and open the way towards $45.50–$46.00. Conversely, a failure to hold above the reclaimed support zone, particularly a decisive break below $41.50, could revive selling pressure and expose the next downside support near $40.” On key levels for the silver rates today in India, the Enrich Money expert said, “The near-term bias remains cautious, with a sustained move above ₹1,58,000 needed to strengthen the recovery and open the way towards ₹1,64,000– ₹1,66,000. Failure to hold the immediate support zone, particularly a decisive break below ₹1,47,000, could revive selling pressure and expose the next downside support near ₹1,42,000.” **Disclaimer: **This story is for educational and informational purposes only.
